correctness.rationale: The finite graph is explicitly normalized by residues {1,3,4,9,10,12}, yielding closed-neighborhood differences of size 3/4 for adjacent/nonadjacent pairs. Every 4-omission failure is exactly a 2+2 selection from an adjacent pair; a complete 13-orbit certificate shows 351 distinct failures, each with exactly one edge witness. A complete 19-orbit certificate shows every 5-omission includes a forbidden tetrad. Monotonicity excludes larger omissions; smaller ones satisfy all constraints, establishing the polynomial and affine-orbit count. The direct Python verifier tested all 8192 sensor masks, and the independently structured C++ checker enumerated all 715 tetrads and 1287 quintuples and the group action, both from actual source files. No infinite statement is asserted.

value.rationale: The Paley graph of order 13 is a canonical prime-order conference graph, with highly uniform local neighborhoods. Exact error-detecting detector reliability is natural and more restrictive than ordinary or outage-tolerant identification. The theorem resolves the precise optimum, every admissible detector size, a unique-witness family of 351 critical omission tetrads and a covering obstruction at five omissions. The seven-orbit structure and all-set multiplicities give informative fault-tolerant sensing benchmarks not implied by generic bounds; no downstream general theorem is necessary for this motivated exact finite classification.
